why: I checked the PASS and FAIL conditions of all five verifier checks against their expect lines. Check 1 tests only exit code 1 and an empty stdout. Check 2 tests `bad config:`, the exact "$d/c.json" string and line 3 / column 3 "in any readable form", and requires no exact wording. Check 3 passes only on OK, meaning it threw and the message contains the path. Check 4 tests `listening on 9000`, exit 0 and a deep equal to `{ port: 9000 }`. Check 5 tests that `npm test` passes at the head and that a test checking for the path fails with the base's src/. The stricter items all sit under "Advisory (not pass/fail)": whether the location is computed or copied from Node's message, the missing-file behaviour, path resolution, and whether the SyntaxError test was kept. No PASS or FAIL condition goes beyond what its expect line requires.
